posts.title: The email. The exhale.
posts.linkedin:
NENEMI just got approved for distribution on the App Store.

I’m still taking that in.

Getting through the submission process took so much out of me. So many steps. So much switching back and forth. I knew what I needed to do, but getting my brain to move from one thing to the next was exhausting.

Then this email came in.

I built NENEMI because I know what it feels like to lose your place and struggle to start again. I wanted a calmer place to come back to.

I built it with Claude Code, with a lot of learning and decisions along the way. And today, it’s approved.

I’m tired. I’m happy. And I’m really proud of this.
posts.instagram:
NENEMI GOT APPROVED. 🖤

I was exhausted getting through the App Store process. The tiny steps. The switching back and forth. Trying to get my brain to go along with what I knew I needed to do.

Then I got this email.

I built a calmer place for brains like mine, with help from Claude Code. Today, Apple approved it for distribution.

Still tired. Very happy. Really fucking proud.

posts.title: Meet NENEMI
posts.line:
A place to
come back to.
posts.linkedin:
Meet NENEMI.

A calm workspace for ADHD and non-linear minds, designed to help you pick up where you left off.

The starting point was a question I kept coming back to: why does returning to my own work take so much work?

This is my attempt to make that part easier. I’ll share more of the actual experience this month.

posts.title: You stepped away
posts.line:
You stepped away.
You can come back.
posts.linkedin:
Sometimes you step away because life interrupts. Sometimes you run out of energy. Sometimes your attention goes somewhere else.

Coming back can be its own hard part.

That’s the moment I keep designing for with NENEMI: helping you find your place again, without a lecture about where you’ve been.

posts.title: What returning means
posts.linkedin:
The idea at the heart of NENEMI is returning.

You leave a thought, a project, or a plan. When you come back, you need enough context to continue.

I want the experience to say: your place is still here.

That’s a design promise I keep working toward.

posts.title: I needed this too
posts.linkedin:
I built NENEMI because I needed something like it in my own life.

I can care deeply about something and still struggle to start. I can understand the steps and still find moving between them exhausting.

That experience shapes the questions I ask when I build. Is this clear? Is this necessary? Does it make coming back easier?

The stepped N is part of that idea: a place you can leave and return to.

Even the small design decisions need a reason to exist.

posts.linkedin:
If the next step still feels too big, we can make it smaller.

Open the document. Write one messy sentence. Say the thought out loud.

The right starting point is the one you can actually reach today.

posts.linkedin:
Getting stuck is something I want the product to make room for.

I don’t want someone to have to figure out how to ask for help before they can get it.

A clear starting point, close at hand. That’s the intent behind the support I’m building into NENEMI.

Sometimes the hardest part is reconstructing what you were thinking before you got interrupted.

That question has shaped so much of NENEMI. What helps you find the thread again?

posts.line:
Built with care.
And a lot of learning.
posts.linkedin:
I built NENEMI with Claude Code.

That still meant deciding what the product should do, what it should feel like, and which parts needed to change.

One of the biggest lessons has been learning to describe the experience I actually want someone to have.

The tool helped me build. The reason for building came from my life.

posts.line:
What felt easy?
What got in the way?

What got in the way?

You don’t need to write a polished review. A small moment of confusion is useful feedback, too. I’m listening.

I want NENEMI to make room for the thought before it’s organized.

You shouldn’t need a finished plan just to capture what’s in your head.

That kind of patience matters.

It’s something I want to carry into what I build.

I’m interested in the real version of your day.

posts.linkedin:

‘I was working on this. The next thing is that.’

It doesn’t have to be organized. It just has to give you a place to begin again.

I want to keep making those moments easier. Your experience helps me see what I’ve missed.
